title: Before the Doors Open
origin: Original fictional proposal, thematically linked to workbook Q3 named ownership under pressure. Not a direct adaptation or answer mapping.

setup.line: One minute before opening, your exhibition team tests its paper city. A hand passes the sensor; a tower should rise once.

setup.speaker: Dev
setup.line: Twice again. One hand, two triggers. I thought I’d fixed that.

setup.speaker: Lio
setup.line: We have the rehearsal recording. It shows the whole movement. But I told people they could come and try it.

setup.speaker: Dev
setup.line: I can stay here and reset it between turns. It might still double-count. Please don’t tell them it’s fixed.

setup.speaker: You
setup.line: I won’t. We’ll explain the fault before anyone tries it. If we show the recording, we’ll say it’s a recording.
Visitors wait outside. At the table are the live controls and a recording of the city working in rehearsal.

choice.prompt: How will you open the exhibit?

actions.label: Run it live
actions.description: Operate the live exhibit, with resets and one visitor at a time.

actions.label: Play the rehearsal
actions.description: Show the recorded demonstration and offer inspection of the mechanism.

live.speaker: You
live.line: Dev, stay with the reset. Lio, one visitor at a time. I’ll explain the fault. Tell me if you need us to stop.

live.speaker: You
live.line: You can try the sensor. It sometimes triggers the tower twice, so we may have to stop and reset. Still want a turn?
The visitor tries the sensor. The tower springs twice. Dev watches it settle; the fault has not gone away.

live.speaker: You
live.line: There it is. Sorry, that should have been one movement. Would you like to reset it with Dev and have another go?
The visitor joins Dev at the reset and tries again. This time, the tower rises once.
The visitor has made the city move. The next person is still waiting. Dev stays by the reset; one good run has not fixed the fault.

rehearsal.speaker: You
rehearsal.line: We’re showing a recorded rehearsal. The live sensor still double-counts. Dev, show how it works. Lio, take requests for a later test.
On the screen, the city moves smoothly from start to finish. On the table, the real mechanism stays still.

rehearsal.speaker: Visitor
rehearsal.line: Can I make it do that? I wanted to try the sensor.

rehearsal.speaker: Dev
rehearsal.line: Not during this demonstration, I’m afraid. I can show you the mechanism, but we haven’t fixed the double trigger yet.
The visitor leans in to inspect the mechanism. The labelled recording plays again. The controls remain unavailable.

briefing.heading: One minute before opening
briefing.text: You lead a student exhibition team. Visitors will use a sensor to move a paper city, but it sometimes triggers the same movement twice. Dev can reset it, not guarantee a fix. Lio has a smooth rehearsal recording, but visitors expected to try the controls themselves. The doors are about to open.
briefing.audioNote: Revised script: captions and room sound. New dialogue recordings are still to come.

live.title: You opened the live prototype.
live.happened: You explained the fault and gave Dev and Lio clear jobs. A visitor helped reset a double count. The queue waited, and the next run was still uncertain.
live.tradeoff: Visitors could participate in the actual work, including its limits. Your team carried the workload of explaining, supervising and resetting an unreliable demonstration.
live.alternative: The clearly labelled recording could show the intended movement reliably. Visitors could inspect the mechanism, but would not control it in that demonstration.
live.question: What failure or queue length would make you stop the live session, and who would have the authority to call that?

rehearsal.title: You showed the recorded rehearsal.
rehearsal.happened: The recording ran smoothly and was labelled as a recording. A visitor could inspect the mechanism but could not make it move.
rehearsal.tradeoff: This gave the team a dependable demonstration without pretending the live fault was fixed. It also removed the hands-on experience the visitor came for.
rehearsal.alternative: A supervised live run could offer participation and useful feedback. It would still bring resets, a waiting queue and a result no one could guarantee.
rehearsal.question: What would you promise about a later live test, and what would you need to verify before making that promise?
